options.text: Use the plus-que-parfait for a habitual past action
Use the passe compose for a habitual past action
Use the present for a habitual past action
Use the imparfait for a habitual past action

questions.explanation: The imparfait describes habitual or repeated past actions. The passe compose would wrongly mark each occurrence as a completed event.

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.learningObjective: Avoid agreement when the object follows
questions.stem: Clerk's note: 'j'ai ecrit la lettre' shows no agreement, so why does the participle not agree?

answer.exemplar: No agreement occurs when the direct object follows the verb, so 'j'ai ecrit la lettre' keeps the participle invariable because la lettre comes after.

questions.explanation: No agreement occurs when the direct object follows the verb. Agreement is triggered only by a preceding direct object.

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.learningObjective: Use plusieurs with a noun

stimulus.body: The file note reads: 'plusieurs documents'. The quantifier precedes the noun directly.

questions.stem: How is plusieurs positioned in that note?

options.text: Place plusieurs after the noun
Place plusieurs before the noun with no de
Place plusieurs with de before the noun
Place plusieurs at the end of the sentence

questions.explanation: Plusieurs precedes the noun directly without de. Adding de would be the error.

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.learningObjective: Explain the effect of ne...que
questions.stem: Clerk's note: 'il ne reste qu'un document' limits the quantity, so how does ne...que affect the sentence?

options.text: It intensifies the statement
It negates the whole statement
It restricts the statement to one item
It adds an extra item

questions.explanation: Ne...que limits the quantity. It does not negate the whole statement.

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.learningObjective: Use the subjonctif after bien que
questions.stem: Clerk's note: 'bien que' opens a clause, so which mood does it demand?

answer.exemplar: Bien que triggers the subjonctif, so 'bien que le document soit signe' uses the subjonctif rather than the indicatif.

questions.explanation: Bien que triggers the subjonctif. The indicatif would treat the conceded point as a plain fact.

questions.learningObjective: Agree the past participle with a preceding direct object
questions.stem: Clerk's note: 'la lettre que j'ai ecrite' shows agreement, so when does the past participle agree?

options.text: It never agrees in compound tenses
It agrees when the direct object follows the verb

questions.explanation: The past participle agrees with a preceding direct object. When the object follows, no agreement occurs.

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.learningObjective: Place a quantifier before a noun correctly
questions.stem: Clerk's note: 'beaucoup de documents' places the quantifier, so how is the quantifier positioned?

answer.exemplar: The quantifier precedes the noun and is followed by de, so 'beaucoup de documents' puts beaucoup before the noun with de linking them.

questions.explanation: Quantifiers like beaucoup precede the noun and take de. Placing de before the quantifier would be the error.
